text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a regression on prod-canary: large heatmap legend interactions cause chart paint lag and sporadic frame drops. Seen on Chrome/Mac and Firefox. Repro steps: open dashboard with ~200 series, hover legend, scrub timeline.

sam: ugh. timeline? is this after the chunk split yesterday?

maria: yes, rollout 22:10 UTC. Client bundle split + new kvcache prefetch heuristics.

jen: can you paste the perf flame or a HAR?

maria: attaching gist of a quick trace: 
```
Main > parse (40ms) > layout (120ms) > paint (220ms)
legend hover handler -> scheduleRender -> re-render legend items
```

noah: 220ms paint on hover sounds like we’re re-rendering whole canvas instead of incremental draw. Did the split change how legend components are imported?

maria: looks like legend rendering moved to async chunk (legend-async) and we now lazily import the color-scale util. On warm load it's fine, but on hover we hit a chunk boundary and then a kvcache miss which stalls the renderer.

sam: that explains the 200-400ms stutter. routing policy might be prefetching the wrong chunk priority. Our prefetch TTL/affinity change could push legend chunk to low priority until first interaction.

jen: can we force-import the legend util in the heatmap bundle as a hotfix? small shim that requires it at top-level to avoid async boundary on hover.

maria: testing a shim now. Quick try: `import './legend-utils';` in heatmap entry — reduces stutter in local canary.

deploy-bot: Deployed canary build 1760012350 to prod-canary (tags: legend-hotfix-shim).

noah: also noticed an interaction with our routing quota: canaries in eu-west got deprioritized by the new routing weight rules, so prefetching didn't happen for some users. If affinity is spread, the warm cache is less likely.

sam: long-term we should either: 1) ensure critical small utils are bundled with their primary consumer, or 2) make prefetch heuristics aware of interaction surfaces (hoverable legend = high priority).

jen: agree. also add a unit check: any async split that affects interactive UX should fail a canary latency gate.

maria: hotfix reduced hover paint from ~220ms to ~30ms in canary. Logging shows fewer kvcache miss spikes. Rolling to a small pct.

noah: PR for permanent fix: move legend-utils into heatmap entry and mark as critical chunk in webpack config. Also make prefetcher flag 'interactive' for elements annotated in JSX. I’ll open it.

sam: one more ask — add telemetry markers: legend-hover-start / legend-render-complete so we can correlate user-facing lags with chunk loads and kvcache miss rates.

jen: +1. can we also add an alert when the 95th percentile hover latency increases by >50ms post-deploy?

maria: added TODOs in the rollout checklist and updated the canary doc. Thanks y’all. :thumbsup:

sam: nice catch. hoping the hotfix keeps charts smooth while we ship the larger routing/prefetch changes.
